s: Hail geopark of a giant ancient caldera and young maar volcanoes · UNESCO 2025
dr: UNESCO Global Geopark 2025; managed by NCVC
te: Where a super-volcano met young craters
ta: حيث يلتقي بركان عملاق قديم بفوهات فتيّة
se: Around the Salma Mountains in Hail, the rocks of an ancient giant caldera sit beside dozens of much younger volcanic craters
sa: حول جبال سلمى في حائل تجاور صخورُ كالديرا عملاقة قديمة عشراتِ الفوهات البركانية الأحدث عمرًا بكثير
desc: A geopark of 3,145 km² about 80 km south-east of Hail, joined to the UNESCO Global Geoparks Network in April 2025 and managed by the National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification. Its core is the Neoproterozoic Salma mega-caldera and batholith, where the Jabal Salma pluton is dated to about 580 Ma and Arabian Shield granite at the western border to about 740 Ma; Salma Mountain rises to 1,380 m. The Pleistocene Hutaymah volcanic field, less than 2 million years old, covers about 900 km² with 77 volcanoes and 119 vent sites, and one of its maars gave an Ar–Ar age of 1.8 ± 0.5 Ma. The park’s geosite material identifies 30 geosites, alongside heritage such as the medieval town of Faid and the Darb Zubaydah pilgrim route.
sig: Brings together one of Arabia’s largest ancient caldera systems and a young maar field in a single protected landscape.

s: Tuwaiq escarpment geopark of Jurassic–Cretaceous sea rocks, caves and fossil reefs · UNESCO 2025
dr: UNESCO Global Geopark 2025; managed by NCVC
te: The old seabed north of Riyadh
se: Near Thadiq, cliffs, caves and fossil coral reefs show that this desert once lay beneath a shallow sea
sa: قرب ثادق تكشف الجروف والكهوف والشعاب المرجانية المتحجّرة أن هذه الصحراء كانت يومًا تحت بحر ضحل
desc: A geopark of about 3,221 km² in Thadiq Governorate, around 140 km north-west of Riyadh, joined to the UNESCO Global Geoparks Network in April 2025 and managed by the National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification. Its Jurassic and Cretaceous rocks were laid down in the shallow Tethys Ocean and are described as equivalent to some of the largest subsurface oil reservoirs in Saudi Arabia, with Quaternary sand dunes and sabkhas above. Slopes of 20 to 40% form an extension of the Tuwaiq Mountain range, cut by canyons, valleys and terraces, with caves and fossil coral reefs. Listed sites include Table Mountain, Khashm Al-Hussan (the highest point), Ghar Al-Amir, Aba Al-Salabikh cave and the Maghatyah seasonal waterfall.
sig: A field classroom for the marine rock layers that hold Saudi Arabia’s oil, exposed along the Tuwaiq escarpment.
disc: Fossil coral reefs in the desert
Rocks equivalent to major oil reservoirs

The geopark’s must-see sites (Aba Al-Salabikh, Al-Jirisi Castle, Jadat Maghatyah, Khashm Al-Hussan, Water Pools) have no published coordinates and are described here

s: Deep maar crater of the Hutaymah volcanic field · Salma Geopark geosite
dr: Hutaymah volcanic field, less than 2 Ma; geosite of Salma UNESCO Global Geopark (2025)
el: About 1.5 km wide and more than 200 m deep
se: When rising magma met groundwater, a huge steam blast tore this deep round crater through an older volcano
sa: حين التقت الصهارة الصاعدة بالمياه الجوفية، شقّ انفجار بخاري هائل هذه الفوهة العميقة المستديرة عبر بركان أقدم منها
desc: A maar crater in the Pleistocene Hutaymah volcanic field east of the Salma Mountains in Hail, about 1.5 km wide and more than 200 m deep. The maar cut through an earlier scoria cone and lava field, recording a change from magmatic to explosive phreatomagmatic eruptions as magma met groundwater. Salma Geopark describes it as a global reference site for monogenetic volcanism. The Hutaymah field is less than 2 million years old and contains 77 volcanoes and 119 vent sites.
sig: One of the clearest examples in Arabia of a maar volcano formed by magma–water explosions.
refs: Németh, K. (2026). The Role of Phreatomagmatism in the Saudi Arabian Neogene–Quaternary Intra-plate Monogenetic Volcanism. In: Németh, K. (ed.), Latest Advances in Volcanology – Volcanoes as Complex Geosystems. IntechOpen. https://doi.org/10.5772/intechopen.1016928
Salma UNESCO Global Geopark. Salma Geological Material for Website (geosite descriptions). https://ksasalmageopark.ncvc.gov.sa/assets/files/Salma-Geological-Material-for-Website.pdf
conf: Coordinates from Németh (2026). Other sources give smaller figures (Arab News 2026: 1.25 km wide and 110 m deep; Saudipedia: 1,200 m and 130 m); the published scientific figures are used. Arabic name follows common Arabic press usage. Timeline is the Pleistocene span of the field; the crater itself is not dated

s: Maar inside the Salma mega-caldera with mantle rocks and a 1.5 km base-surge section
dr: About 1 Ma (inferred); geosite of Salma UNESCO Global Geopark (2025)
el: Base-surge succession about 1.5 km long and 30 m thick
se: Repeated steam explosions here hurled up rocks from the Earth’s mantle and stacked thick ash layers inside an ancient caldera
sa: قذفت الانفجارات البخارية المتكررة هنا صخورًا من وشاح الأرض، وكدّست طبقات رماد سميكة داخل كالديرا قديمة
desc: A maar of the Pleistocene Hutaymah volcanic field that erupted inside an intra-mountain basin of the resurgent granophyre rocks of the Salma mega-caldera in Hail. It records repeated maar formation along fissures in a complex monogenetic system, and phreatomagmatic explosions carried mantle xenoliths to the surface. Its exposed base-surge succession is about 1.5 km long and 30 m thick, described by Salma Geopark as one of the best in the world. Németh (2026) infers an age of about 1 million years.
sig: A rare exposure of base-surge deposits and mantle fragments that shows how maar volcanoes interact with rugged mountain terrain.
refs: Németh, K. (2026). The Role of Phreatomagmatism in the Saudi Arabian Neogene–Quaternary Intra-plate Monogenetic Volcanism. In: Németh, K. (ed.), Latest Advances in Volcanology – Volcanoes as Complex Geosystems. IntechOpen. https://doi.org/10.5772/intechopen.1016928
Salma UNESCO Global Geopark. Salma Geological Material for Website (geosite descriptions). https://ksasalmageopark.ncvc.gov.sa/assets/files/Salma-Geological-Material-for-Website.pdf
conf: Coordinates from Németh (2026) mark a tuff-ring outcrop, not the crater centre. Age is inferred in the source, so t0 and t1 are the same single value. Arabic name is a transliteration (Németh also spells it An Nay’yn, or Jubb)

s: Wide sediment-filled maar with mantle rocks, and the old village on its rim · Salma Geopark geosites
dr: Formed more than a million years ago; three geosites of Salma UNESCO Global Geopark (2025)
el: Village of about 5,000 people about 90 km south-east of Hail
te: The village on the volcano’s rim
se: Tabah village sits on the rim of a wide old volcanic crater whose floor is slowly sinking
sa: تقع قرية طابة على حافة فوهة بركانية قديمة واسعة، يهبط قاعها ببطء
desc: A wide, relatively flat maar of the Hutaymah volcanic field near the Salma Mountains, partly filled with sediment and ringed by a continuous tuff ring, with visible subsidence of the crater floor. Salma Geopark lists it as a global reference site for mantle xenoliths, and a separate geosite shows the remains of a pre-maar scoria cone and basaltic plug rocks. Németh (2026) infers it formed over a million years ago. Tabah village, among the oldest settlements in the Hail region, was built on the crater rim in pre-Islamic times, lies about 90 km south-east of Hail and has about 5,000 inhabitants; the 1983 earthquakes cracked its buildings.
sig: A place where a volcanic crater, mantle rocks and a long-lived village share one landscape.
refs: Németh, K. (2026). The Role of Phreatomagmatism in the Saudi Arabian Neogene–Quaternary Intra-plate Monogenetic Volcanism. In: Németh, K. (ed.), Latest Advances in Volcanology – Volcanoes as Complex Geosystems. IntechOpen. https://doi.org/10.5772/intechopen.1016928
Salma UNESCO Global Geopark. Salma Geological Material for Website (geosite descriptions). https://ksasalmageopark.ncvc.gov.sa/assets/files/Salma-Geological-Material-for-Website.pdf
Arab News (2024). Saudi village built atop volcanic crater attracts tourists. 26 June 2024. https://www.arabnews.pk/node/2538306/saudi-arabia
conf: One record for three geosites: Tabah Crater maar (SA-A7), Tabah Crater archaeological site (SA-A6, actually a pre-maar scoria cone and plug) and Tabah Heritage Village (SA-A8). Coordinates from Németh (2026) for the maar; no separate coordinates are published for the village. Population differs between sources (Salma Geopark: about 9,000; Arab News 2024: about 5,000). Timeline is a broad estimate from the field age (less than 2 Ma) and the inferred age (over 1 Ma)

n: Jabal Qidr historic scoria cone (Harrat Khaybar)
na: المخروط البركاني التاريخي لجبل القدر (حرة خيبر)
s: Youngest eruption of Harrat Khaybar, whose lava reached Bronze Age desert kites · IUGS Geoheritage Site
el: Cone about 400 m high; crater about 200 m deep and 300 m wide
te: The volcano that buried hunters’ traps
se: Jabal Qidr is the youngest volcano of Harrat Khaybar, and its black lava flowed over ancient desert kites
sa: جبل القدر أحدث براكين حرة خيبر، وقد زحفت حممه السوداء فوق مصائد الصحراء القديمة
desc: A large scoria cone in Harrat Khaybar rising about 400 m above its surroundings, with a crater about 200 m deep and 300 m wide. It is the youngest eruption in the largest intracontinental bimodal volcanic field of the Arabian Peninsula and lies on a roughly north–south fissure that fed tube-fed pahoehoe lava flows. The eruption reached sub-Plinian to violent Strombolian intensity, spreading an ash plain at least 20 km from the vent, and its lava flows reached Bronze Age desert kites. It was named one of the IUGS First 100 Geological Heritage Sites in 2022.
sig: A globally recognised record of young explosive basalt volcanism that overlapped with human occupation of Arabia.
disc: Ash plain at least 20 km wide
refs: Németh, K. & Moufti, M.R. (2022). The historic scoria cone of the Jabal Qidr, Saudi Arabia. IUGS Geological Heritage Sites. https://iugs-geoheritage.org/geoheritage_sites/historic-scoria-cone-of-the-jabal-qidr/

Németh, K. & Moufti, M.R. (2017). Geoheritage Values of a Mature Monogenetic Volcanic Field in Intra-continental Settings: Harrat Khaybar, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Geoheritage 9(3), 311–328. https://doi.org/10.1007/s12371-017-0243-2
conf: Coordinates from the IUGS site page. The IUGS page gives no eruption date; the timeline is the Holocene span it lists. Distinct from the White Volcanoes of Harrat Khaybar already on the map (about 14 km away)

s: Sand-dune reserve in Al-Qassim for houbara bustards and desert wildlife
te: A sea of sand kept for the houbara
ta: بحر من الرمال محميّ لطائر الحبارى
se: Rolling dunes in Al-Qassim protected so houbara bustards, fennec foxes and sand cats can live safely
sa: كثبان متموجة في القصيم تُحمى ليعيش فيها طائر الحبارى وثعلب الفنك والقط الرملي بأمان
desc: A protected area of 2,036.1 km² of sand dunes in Dariyyah Governorate, south-west of Buraydah in Al-Qassim, and the only reserve in the province. Vegetation includes Haloxylon salicornicum, Calligonum and Lycium shawii, and the reserve is a habitat for the houbara bustard, hyena and wolf. A preliminary 2023 survey recorded 15 animal species over about two months, including 8 birds and 3 mammals (fennec fox, sand cat and gerbil).
sig: A core dune habitat in central Arabia used for houbara bustard conservation.
ex: National Center for Wildlife; GSC BPS (2023)

s: Saudi Arabia’s first national park, from Red Sea mangroves to juniper peaks at 3,200 m
el: 6,490.7 km², from sea level to 3,200 m
te: From the sea to the juniper peaks
se: A huge park that climbs from coastal mangroves through acacia woodland to cool juniper forests on the mountain tops
sa: منتزه شاسع يصعد من أشجار القرم على الساحل عبر غابات السَّمُر إلى غابات العرعر الباردة على قمم الجبال
desc: A national park of 6,490.7 km² near Abha in Asir, established in 1981 and spanning elevations from 0 m at the Red Sea coast to 3,200 m on the mountain peaks. The coast receives under 100 mm of rain a year with a mean temperature of about 29 °C, while the highlands receive under 250 mm with about 19 °C. Vegetation runs from mangroves and sparse coastal desert through Acacia woodland and thorn scrub on the western foothills to Juniperus procera woodland above about 1,600 m. Key Biodiversity Area assessments list Dracaena serrulata (Endangered) and Euphorbia ammak (Vulnerable).
sig: Protects a complete altitudinal sequence of south-west Arabian habitats in one park.
refs: Protected Planet. ‘Asir National Park (WDPA 864). https://www.protectedplanet.net/864

s: AlUla canyon reserve restoring acacia woodland, gazelles and oryx · IUCN Green List
dr: Nature reserve 2019; renamed national park after IUCN Green List listing (announced January 2025)
te: Canyons where the wild is coming back
se: Red canyons near AlUla where gazelles, oryx and ibex roam again, as the land is prepared for the Arabian leopard
sa: أودية حمراء قرب العُلا تجوبها الظباء والمها والوعول من جديد، فيما تُهيَّأ الأرض لعودة النمر العربي
desc: A protected area of about 1,540 km² in the canyons north-east of AlUla, managed by the Royal Commission for AlUla since 2019. It protects acacia woodland and native species such as gazelles and the Arabian oryx, and is home to Arabian wolves and Nubian ibex, with restoration central to its management. It is linked to RCU’s programme for captive breeding and reintroduction of the Arabian leopard. Sharaan was added to the IUCN Green List in the 2024–2025 listings, assessed against 17 criteria, and was renamed Sharaan National Park; less than 10% of the park is open to motorised tourism.
sig: A flagship of ecological restoration in north-west Arabia and one of few Saudi sites on the IUCN Green List.

n: Imam Abdulaziz bin Mohammed Royal Reserve (Rawdat Khuraim)
na: محمية الإمام عبدالعزيز بن محمد الملكية (روضة خريم)
s: Royal reserve north-east of Riyadh built around the green meadow of Rawdat Khuraim
dr: Royal reserve 2018 (from Rawdat Khuraim Reserve and surrounding areas)
el: About 11,300 km²; Rawdat Khuraim about 18 km long
te: The green meadow of the desert
se: After rain, the Rawdat Khuraim basin turns green and becomes a haven for oryx, gazelles and ostriches
sa: بعد المطر تكتسي روضة خريم بالخضرة وتغدو ملاذًا للمها والظباء والنعام
desc: A royal reserve of about 11,300 km² in north-eastern Riyadh Province, about 100 km from Riyadh, created by royal decree in 2018 from the Rawdat Khuraim Reserve and its surroundings. Rawdat Khuraim is a depression about 18 km long and 2.5 km wide on the south-western edge of the Dahna desert, fed by valleys including Khawish, Thilan and Al-Thumamah; the original reserve covered about 45 km². About 132 native plant species are estimated in the protected area, and wildlife includes Arabian oryx, gazelles, red-necked ostrich and steppe eagles. The reserve’s development authority also oversees King Khalid Royal Reserve.
sig: Protects one of central Arabia’s most botanically diverse rawdas and the rangelands around it.
